lines.text: Kau. अत्यागेपि &c.—Even though the body is not cast off i. e.
he will not have to wait for a second birth. संपत्स्यते—see
Kum. II. 54 &c. सुखं संपत्स्यते v. l.—In this case संपद् must be
understood as used transitively.

transcription.note: The Sanskrit readings are somewhat unclear.

lines.text: Sl. 92. कौपीनं—a small piece of cloth used to cover the
privities. जर्जरतर—extremely ragged. चिन्ता act of contemplation.
Also a thought about (i. e. a wish for) a secluded place; ध्वस्ताशेष
&c.—delighted at the total destruction of egotism and errors;
or मदप्रमादाः errors arising from egotism or pride.

transcription.note: Some Sanskrit words are difficult to distinguish.

lines.text: Sl. 93. ब्रह्माण्डं मण्डलीमात्रं—v. l.—a mere circular body i. e.
which is limited in space and not अपरिच्छिन्न like Brahman.
This is perhaps a better reading. शफरी—a small fish. क्षुब्धता
जातु जायते—a question implying the negative answer in itself—
‘Is ever agitation produced &c. ?’—‘Never.’ जातु ever, at
any time.

transcription.note: The Sanskrit in the first and third lines is indistinct.

lines.text: Sl. 94. मा स्म भूः-मा sometimes followed by स्म, is used with
a form of the Imperf. or Aorist with the aug. अ dropped. Cf.
क्लैब्यं मास्म गमः पार्थ &c. Bhg. II. 3. भोगेभ्यः—‘the dat. by
स्पृहेरीप्सितः Pân. I. 4. 36. In the case of the root स्पृह् the object
desired is put in the dative case. स्पृहयालु—from स्पृह् + आलु
by ‘स्पृहेर्गृधि पतिदयिनिद्रातन्द्राश्रद्धाभ्य आलुच्—’ Pân. III. 2.
358; so गृधयालु, पतयालु &c. स्यूत—stitched; p. p. p. of सिव् 4 cl.
भिक्षासक्तु—barley-flour ( obtained by ) begging. Cf. infra Mis.

transcription.note: The grammatical quotation and several Sanskrit forms are hard to read; lines 6 and 8 contain detached vowel marks.

lines.text: Sl. 95. उपधानम्—pillow; fr. उप + धा + ल्युट् ( अन ). वितान—
m. n. a canopy. वितन्यते इति fr. तन् with वि + घञ् ( अ ). विरतिवनिता-
Cf. infra mis. 39, कुर्वत करुणामैत्रीप्रज्ञावधूजनसंगमम् where करुणा, मैत्री
and प्रज्ञा are likewise called wives. सुखम्—an adv. here. अतनु
&c.—from the adj. तनु the fem. forms are तनु or तन्वी. भूति has
two meanings viz. ( 1 ) ‘prosperity’ as applicable to the king
and (2) ‘ashes’ as applicable to the Muni. Cf. Mis. Sl. 31. infra.

transcription.note: The quoted Sanskrit in line 3 is indistinct.

lines.text: Sl. 96. स्वायत्त &c.—जितेन्द्रियः whose movements are under
control; who practises self-restraint. आस्यूत &c.—an एकदेशी
अन्वय. संप्रोत v. l. sewn together, patched with. समसुखभोग &c.—

transcription.note: The final Sanskrit expression is difficult to read.
